subject: paediatrics
title: Patterns of inheritance and genetic syndromes in children

steps.tx: Inheritance is read from the pedigree pattern across three generations. **Autosomal dominant** disease passes vertically with an affected parent and half risk to each child, **autosomal recessive** disease appears horizontally with carrier parents, quarter risk, and increased consanguinity risk. X linked disease passes through carrier mothers to sons, mitochondrial disease passes from mother to all children, and imprinting causes Prader Willi or Angelman depending on parent of origin. Mosaicism, anticipation from triplet expansion, and quoted recurrence numbers complete counselling.
steps.say: The pedigree pattern reveals how a disorder passes through families. Dominant disease appears in successive generations vertically. Recessive disease appears horizontally among siblings with carrier parents. Mitochondrial disorders pass only through the mother. Careful pedigree drawing helps the counsellor quote recurrence risks accurately.

steps.tx: Syndromes are recognised by combining facial, skeletal, skin, and internal features. **Marfan syndrome** causes tall stature, arachnodactyly, lens subluxation, and aortic root dilatation from FBN1, while **neurofibromatosis type 1** causes cafe au lait spots, freckling, neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, and optic glioma. Achondroplasia causes rhizomelic shortening and trident hand, Noonan syndrome causes webbed neck and pulmonary stenosis, Williams syndrome causes elfin facies and supravalvular aortic stenosis, and Fragile X causes macroorchidism with autism. Genetic panels and exome testing confirm.
steps.say: Syndromes become recognisable when features are combined. Long fingers and lens displacement suggest Marfan syndrome. Multiple pigmented spots and skin tumours suggest neurofibromatosis. Short limbs with a trident hand suggest achondroplasia. Genetic testing confirms the clinical impression and guides family screening.

steps.tx: Management is surveillance and prevention of syndrome specific complications. **Marfan syndrome** needs **echocardiography** of the aortic root, beta blocker therapy, and activity limits, NF1 needs optic pathway and plexiform neurofibroma watch, and achondroplasia may need foramen magnum decompression. Noonan and Williams syndromes need cardiac echoes, Williams hypercalcaemia needs dietary care, Fragile X needs autism support, and tuberous sclerosis seizures may need vigabatrin. Annual system reviews, eye checks, growth charts, and school learning support keep care coordinated.
steps.say: Management focuses on preventing complications that each syndrome predicts. The aortic root needs regular imaging in Marfan syndrome. Vision and tumour growth need surveillance in neurofibromatosis. Cardiac lesions need echocardiography in several syndromes. School support helps children whose learning is affected by their condition.

steps.tx: This echocardiogram shows a markedly dilated **aortic root** at the sinuses of Valsalva measuring 5.6 centimetres beside the left ventricle, left atrium, and mitral valve. In Marfan syndrome, progressive root dilatation risks dissection, so serial **echocardiography**, beta blocker therapy, and activity restriction are central exam points. The image teaches that tall stature and arachnodactyly are not cosmetic clues alone, because the life threatening lesion is inside the aorta.
steps.say: This ultrasound shows a greatly enlarged aortic root beside the cardiac chambers. Aortic dilatation is the dangerous complication of Marfan syndrome. Serial echocardiography tracks root size before dissection occurs. Treatment slows progression and activity advice reduces risk. The image connects external Marfan features with life threatening internal disease.

steps.tx: Genetic counselling quotes risks, offers testing, and respects family values. Recurrence is half for dominant and quarter for recessive disorders, prenatal options include **chorionic villus sampling**, amniocentesis, and noninvasive testing, and **carrier testing** cascades through siblings. Consanguinity is discussed respectfully, preconception folate and rubella planning are offered, and disclosure uses language the child can understand with assent. Predictive testing in children is usually deferred, insurance discrimination is guarded, and pedigrees and family clinic registers are maintained carefully.
steps.say: Counselling translates genetic risk into choices families understand. Dominant disorders carry a one in two recurrence risk. Recessive disorders carry a one in four risk with carrier parents. Prenatal testing offers information before birth for some families. Predictive testing in childhood is usually deferred to protect future autonomy.
